header: One panel at a time, behind tabs
lead: Two to eight rich-text panels behind a row of tabs. Without JavaScript, the panels show as a stack of sections with headings.

panels.title: Without JavaScript
panels.bodytext: All panels are rendered and none starts hidden. The page is longer and the tabs do nothing. Every word can still be read, printed, searched and indexed.

panels.title: With JavaScript
panels.bodytext: The shared script turns the row into tabs and shows one panel at a time. The arrow keys move between tabs, and Home and End jump to the first and last. The row counts as a single stop when you tab through the page.

panels.title: When to use it
panels.bodytext: Use it for instructions per operating system, one product for two audiences, prices per region, or answers for private and business customers. If readers work through the panels in order, use an accordion.
